prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro: urban CBTC railway (peak/off-peak/engineering hours). CBTC handles separation, movement authority (MA), regulation. Actors: Line Traffic Controller (monitors, authorizes, incidents; uses Lantern displays, no vital intervention); Revenue Train Operator (cab; acknowledgements to Atlas via monitored path); field staff; Signal Maintenance Engineer, alias Maple (uses Quarry, Maintenance Diagnostic Server); Cyber Security Officer (access, keys). Elements: - Metro Operations Control System, alias Lantern: regulation, alarms, commands; displays zone status, radio alarms, supervision states; sends Crew Login Token Bundle. - North District Zone Controller, alias Marble (north line/turnback; requests East Junction routes only if consistent with MA and approach profile). South District Zone Controller, alias Orchid (south line/turnback; West Junction, flank protection, conflicting-movement locking). Both send MA to onboard; receiving zone validates route state, train identity, boundary track section before extending authority. - East Junction Interlocking, alias Falcon; West Junction Interlocking: report switch state, occupancy, route locking to zone controller via vital interfaces; retain final authority for point movement/locking, route locking, section release. Route available only when points detected, locked, proved. Junction boundary by route state, point position, track vacancy, not chainage. - Wayside supervision compares indications, positions, radio state; mismatch withholds/shortens MA. - Atlas Onboard Controller, alias Kestrel: ATP, MA, speed, doors; modes initialization, protected manual, ATO, fallback, cutout; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log; at boundary confirms position from Dual Channel Odometer before accepting new authority; radio loss falls back to last validated MA. - Dual Channel Odometer: divergence degrades mode. - Propulsion/brake interface. - Train Radio Modem: bearer over Saffron, make-before-break. - Wayside Radio Access Network, alias Saffron: overlapping coverage; sends Radio Handover Audit File each interval. - Safety Data Communication Network: vital messages, authenticated; sends Clock Drift Sample Report. - Cryptographic Key Management Appliance. - Maintenance Diagnostic Server: receives non-vital radio/network health summaries. - Service Timetable Server, Passenger Information Gateway: non-vital, isolated from protection paths. - Voice Dispatch Console: not substitute for safety data. - Platform Screen Door Controller: permitted indications only; cannot override MA.

New part:
S083: A requested route is not incorporated into a movement authority until the associated overlap and flank conditions are confirmed as protected.
S084: If the interlocking reports loss of point correspondence after a route has been granted, the affected movement authority is shortened or withdrawn according to the safe braking envelope.
S085: Axle counter clear and occupied indications are used as independent wayside evidence for route availability and for the continued integrity of route locking.
S086: Where axle counter occupation conflicts with the train location estimated by the CBTC system, the more restrictive state is applied until the discrepancy is resolved.
S087: East Junction Interlocking sends the Axle Counter Reset Request under the configured degraded-mode reset procedure.
S088: Reset processing is inhibited while any associated route remains locked or while a train is approaching the affected detection section.
S089: Maple verifies local track clearance evidence and records the result before authorising restoration of normal route setting after a detection anomaly.
S090: West Junction Interlocking sends the Route Release Exception List when normal sectional release cannot be completed within the configured timing rules.
S091: The zone controller treats any release exception as a retained hazard until the affected path is excluded from new movement authorities.
S092: Platform approach protection is enforced by combining the active route state with train stopping accuracy supervision near the platform berth.
S093: The Platform Screen Door Controller provides door closed and locked indications to the supervising wayside systems, but those indications do not replace interlocking route proof.
S094: If platform door readiness is absent, the approaching train may be held outside the platform stopping window even when the junction route is otherwise proved.
S095: The Atlas Onboard Controller uses the token bundle to validate that onboard operating context is current before accepting supervised route-related data.
S096: Train Radio Modem messages carrying route status are exchanged through Wayside Radio Access Network paths with sequence monitoring and timeout handling.
S097: Safety Data Communication Network paths between the zone controllers and the interlockings are configured for deterministic delivery of vital state changes and command acknowledgements.
S098: Metro Operations Control System displays the commanded route, locked route, point state, and track occupancy state as separate indications so that control staff can identify mismatches.
S099: A Line Traffic Controller may request a regulating action, but the request is executed only if the interlocking and CBTC protection rules agree that the route remains safe.
S100: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server records route command outcomes, point operation timing, and detection transitions for later engineering review without participating in vital decisions.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
response: {"summary":"Greenvale Metro: urban CBTC railway (peak/off-peak/engineering hours); CBTC handles separation, movement authority (MA), regulation. Actors: Line Traffic Controller (monitors, incidents, uses Lantern; regulating requests executed only if interlocking and CBTC rules agree route safe; no vital intervention); Revenue Train Operator (cab; acknowledgements to Atlas via monitored path); field staff; Signal Maintenance Engineer, alias Maple (uses Maintenance Diagnostic Server; verifies and records track clearance evidence before restoring normal route setting after detection anomaly); Cyber Security Officer (access, keys). Elements: - Metro Operations Control System, alias Lantern: regulation, alarms, commands; displays commanded route, locked route, point state, occupancy, zone/radio/supervision states separately; sends Crew Login Token Bundle to Atlas. - North District Zone Controller, alias Marble (north, East Junction routes only if consistent with MA). South District Zone Controller, alias Orchid (south, West Junction, flank, conflict locking). Both send MA onboard; receiving zone validates route, train identity, boundary section before extending. Route enters MA only after overlap/flank protected; point correspondence loss shortens/withdraws MA per braking envelope; release exception is retained hazard until path excluded. - East Junction Interlocking, alias Falcon (sends Axle Counter Reset Request in degraded-mode procedure; reset inhibited while route locked or train approaching); West Junction Interlocking (sends Route Release Exception List when sectional release times out). Both report points, occupancy, locking via vital interfaces; final authority over points, locking, release; route needs points detected, locked, proved. - Axle counters: independent evidence; conflict with CBTC location applies more restrictive state. - Wayside supervision: mismatch withholds/shortens MA. - Atlas Onboard Controller, alias Kestrel: ATP, MA, speed, doors; modes initialization, protected manual, ATO, fallback, cutout; validates context via token bundle; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log; confirms position from Dual Channel Odometer (divergence degrades mode) at boundary; radio loss uses last validated MA. - Train Radio Modem: via Wayside Radio Access Network, alias Saffron (make-before-break, sequence/timeout monitoring; sends Radio Handover Audit File). - Safety Data Communication Network: authenticated, deterministic vital delivery; sends Clock Drift Sample Report. - Cryptographic Key Management Appliance. - Maintenance Diagnostic Server: records health, route outcomes, point timing, detection; non-vital. - Service Timetable Server, Passenger Information Gateway, Voice Dispatch Console: non-vital. - Platform Screen Door Controller: sends door closed/locked indications to wayside; not route proof; absent readiness holds train outside platform."}
